General Strike Disrupts Supply Chains Across Bangladesh; ACI Ltd Among Firms Impacted

A nationwide general strike brought economic activity across Bangladesh to a near standstill on Tuesday, as workers from multiple sectors walked off the job demanding wage increases and improved labor protections. The industrial action, organized by a coalition of labor unions, has disrupted transportation, logistics, manufacturing, and retail operations throughout the country.

ACI Ltd, one of the country’s largest diversified conglomerates, confirmed significant operational delays due to the strike. "Our supply chain and distribution networks have been severely affected, with shipments delayed by up to 48 hours," said Shafique Rahman, spokesperson for ACI Ltd. "We are monitoring the situation closely and urge all parties to resolve the dispute for the sake of the broader economy."

Road and port transport have been the most visibly impacted, with Dhaka’s main container depot reporting a 60% drop in throughput since early morning. Shipments of food, pharmaceuticals, and industrial goods from key firms such as ACI Ltd and Bengal Textiles have been halted or rerouted. The Bangladesh Garment Exporters’ Association estimated that the industry is losing approximately $35 million per day during the strike.

Trade union representatives state that the walkout is a response to stagnant wages amid rising inflation. "Workers can no longer afford basic necessities," said Mohammad Yunus, a labor leader. "We have been left with no choice but to take this action."

Analysts warn that a prolonged strike could destabilize the country’s export sector, which is still recovering from the global pandemic. "If the disruption continues for more than a week, there will be knock-on effects on international shipment schedules and supplier contracts," said Farhana Alam, an economist at Dhaka Policy Institute.

At the time of writing, negotiations between union leaders and government officials are ongoing, with no clear resolution in sight.
